name: creamy white beans and polenta
instructions:
Creamy white beans over cooked polenta — the combo: COOKED POLENTA, HEAVY CREAM, SHALLOT/GARLIC, WHITE BEANS, and PARSLEY.

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. COOK THE POLENTA ([[polenta]] — the Bob's Red Mill ratios with the salt corrected).
2. BEANS: soften shallot + garlic, add the white beans, pour in the heavy cream and warm through.
3. Serve the creamy beans over the polenta, with PARSLEY to finish.

NO PARMESAN, NO LEMON — both confirmed to make it worse (see notes).
notes:
=== THE RECIPE THE RETIRED ONE WAS LOOKING FOR ===

This is what the retired italian-no-tomato-white-beans (the garlic-breadcrumb creamy white beans, retired September 2026 for never achieving exit velocity) was really trying to be: creamy white beans AND POLENTA. The polenta is the missing starch underneath the creamy beans.

=== PARMESAN AND LEMON MAKE IT WORSE — CONFIRMED ===

Both CLASHING, confirmed by cooking. Notable inversion from the retired predecessor, where parmesan was primary (the cream's savory anchor) and lemon was the sicilian-crossover brightener — neither survives the move onto polenta.
